Santa Clause. The reason I say this is because I still remember... and it made me not trust my parents for the rest of my life, and I resented them for it.

I was 6-8 years old and I would write Santa every year with my wishlist and my mother would send Santa the letter. I remember staying up until about 5 a.m in the morning. I walked downstairs and my mother and sister were awake cooking food (We had a lot of people come to our house for Christmas Dinner). There were already presents under the tree, but I knew it came from family and Santa came later to drop more off.

I fell asleep and we got up around 6:30 am because of that excitement you feel about getting presents. When I went downstairs, there was only one extra present that I saw and it was a big present (though it was a doll house for my little sister). I put two and two together and figured out Santa was a lie.

Eventually my parents told me the truth and from that point on, I always questioned whether they knew what they were doing or not. I lost trust in the ability to tell the truth and manage their lives.

This probably made me question my faith as well, since we went to church every Sunday and I started asking questions and eventually became an atheist in High School.

That's one thing I'm glad my parents never lied to me about. Santa was always sort of a mascot character for Christmas. Like how no one believes in the Easter Bunny. Of course their reasoning was that I should know that Christmas is really about Jesus...
It's REALLY about a different made up mascot!
If you still believed in Santa at 8, you've got bigger problems.
